newsitem.title: JAPAN: Saturn to start Japan sales on April 5.
newsitem.headline: Saturn to start Japan sales on April 5.

text.p: Saturn Japan, a division of General Motors Japan Ltd, said on Thursday it will start selling right-hand-drive Saturns in Japan on April 5.
The cars, to be produced by GM's Saturn division at its plant in Spring Hill, Tennessee, will the first U.S.-made right-hand-drive cars sold in Japan by the the world's largest automaker.
Saturn Japan said prices would range from 1.56 million yen ($12,700) for the SL2 Sedan to 1.72 million yen ($14,000) and for SC2 Coupe.
"I am convinced our cars have the right performance, features and quality to fully meet the expectations of Japanese customers," Saturn Japan general director Keith Wicks said in a statement.

The Japan Automobile Importers' Association announced on Thursday that while sales of imported vehicles in Japan rose 8.6 percent in February from a year earlier to 36,759 units, sales of GM cars fell 31.5 percent to 1,364 units. ($1=122)
